text: recommended by 860 Antivirals NICE17 for postexposure prophylaxis in persons 13 years of age or older at high risk of complications of influenza. Neither drug is recommended for seasonal prophylaxis of influenza. For most people treatment of influenza is largely sympto- matic and supportive. However, antivirals may be used for the treatment of vaccinated or unvaccinated individuals who develop symptoms. Amantadine and rimantadine have been shown to reduce the duration of uncomplicated influenza A infection when given within 48 hours of the onset of symptoms. These drugs may be considered for pa- tients at high risk of complications. Treatment failures may be due to the rapid emergence of drug resistance.11,13,18 They are not effective against influenza B or the avian in- fluenza H5N1 strain.11 Oseltamivir and zanamivir given within 48 hours of the onset of symptoms are active against both influenza A and B viruses and reduce the du- ration of uncomplicated influenza by about 1 day in healthy adults and adolescents. Data is limited and incon- clusive for all 4 drugs in terms of effectiveness when given to individuals at high risk of complications of influenza. Neuraminidase inhibitors have several advantages com- pared with amantadine, including reduced viral resistance, additional efficacy against influenza B, fewer adverse ef- fects (including CNS effects), and reduction in clinical symptoms. Viral strains resistant to amantadine and riman- tadine generally remain susceptible to neuraminidase in- hibitors.14,15,18,19 In the UK, oseltamivir and zanamivir are recommended20 for the treatment of adults at risk of complications of influ- enza who can start treatment within 48 hours of the onset of symptoms. Only oseltamivir is recommended for the treatment of influenza in children. In the UK NICE does not recommend the use of amantadine for the treatment of influenza. In the USA, the Advisory Committee on Immu- nization Practices10 and the American Academy of Pediatrics16 recommend oseltamivir or zanamivir for treat- ment of acute illness caused by influenza A or B. Neurami- nidase inhibitors have also been effective against some strains of avian influenza in animal studies and may be considered for both prophylaxis and treatment of suspect- ed H5N1 disease.2,11,16 1.
